tier_reason: Founder decision 2026-09-03: deprioritized alongside react. Neither Chatwoot nor Intercom -- the closest comparable competitors at Erghi's stage -- maintain framework wrappers around their vanilla widget. Kept as real, working, tested code; not getting further active build investment. Bug fixes and security issues still land.
verification_method: Read angular/src/lib/services/*.ts directly. Unlike react, angular has NO dependency on @erghi-ai/sdk (angular/package.json:37-40 lists only @microsoft/signalr and tslib) -- it reimplements auth/chat as its own HttpClient calls (angular/src/lib/services/auth.service.ts, chat.service.ts). That is a real, independent client, not a thin hook layer, and it carries its own drift risk: it can silently diverge from the platform's wire contract in ways react structurally cannot.

auth.evidence: angular/src/lib/services/auth.service.ts:47,55,68,105,116 (login/register/refresh/logout/me); no forgotPassword/resetPassword/verifyEmail calls anywhere in the service.

chat.evidence: chat.service.ts has no send-typing call, but signalr.service.ts:134-136's sendTyping() invokes 'SendTyping' on the hub directly.

widgets.evidence: angular/src/lib/services/chat.service.ts:96-120 -- actually the most complete widget CRUD of any SDK (list/get/create/update/delete), ahead of javascript which only has create.

realtime.protocol: signalr-hub-over-websocket (own implementation, angular/src/lib/services/signalr.service.ts, not shared with javascript)

notes: Ironically ahead of javascript on widget CRUD and has a de-novo working SignalR client -- this is real, non-trivial code, which is exactly why the founder called it 'not worth removing' even while deprioritizing further investment. The maintenance-tier risk here is specifically the independent-reimplementation one: because it does not depend on @erghi-ai/sdk, a platform auth/tenancy change (e.g. a new required header, a token-refresh contract change) must be manually ported into this package's services and will NOT be caught just by bumping @erghi-ai/sdk's version. Any agent touching auth/tenancy on the platform should grep this package's services explicitly, not assume javascript's fix covers it.
